headline: Majors hold their 200-day lines while the day's candle gets sold hard
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the one steady thing on an otherwise ugly day. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day averages with golden crosses intact, while DOGE and ADA sit below theirs with no golden cross. That's five of seven majors still in a technical uptrend structurally, even as every single one of them is red today. BTC is down 3.3% on the day and down 5.2% on the week, but up 19.2% on the month. ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and ADA all show the same pattern: red day, red week, green month. That's not noise, that's a real divergence between the medium-term trend (still up) and the short-term tape (getting hit).

Momentum backs up the idea that this is a pullback inside an uptrend rather than a trend break, at least for now. RSI-14 across the majors sits in a tight 44-54 band, which is neutral territory, not oversold, not overheated. MACD is below signal on every single asset in the set, meaning short-term momentum has rolled over even as price stays above the long-term average. That's a textbook cooling-off signature: the trend hasn't broken, but the thrust behind it has faded. XRP's move stands out from the pack: down 9.5% on the day versus BTC's 3.3%, on 98.3% realized volatility, the highest of the group. When one asset moves three times the leader's daily change, that's dispersion, not a uniform selloff.

Positioning tells a mixed story depending on where you look. BTC funding on OKX is 6.1% annualized, mildly positive, meaning longs are still paying shorts to hold their bets, a modest tax on optimism. ETH funding has flipped negative to -0.2% annualized, and SOL is meaningfully negative at -6.5%, meaning shorts are now paying longs there, a sign the crowd has leaned bearish enough to invert the fee. Long/short account ratios are heavily skewed long across the board (BTC 1.8, ETH 2.11, SOL 2.39, XRP 3.02, DOGE 4.71), so retail accounts are still positioned long even as funding on some pairs suggests otherwise. Liquidations in the last few hours lean toward longs getting hurt in BTC ($603K longs vs $825K shorts) and especially ETH ($151K longs vs $1.08M shorts), while SOL, XRP, and DOGE show the opposite, longs barely touched, shorts wiped. Crowded long positioning meeting a down day is exactly the kind of setup that produces one-sided liquidation prints.

Flows add a layer of tension. BTC spot ETFs printed a net outflow of $73.9M on 15 Sep 2026, and the five-session net is a larger outflow of $330.1M, same direction both windows, so that's a real short-run trend, not a one-day blip. ETH ETFs, by contrast, show a $49.5M outflow on the day but a five-session net inflow of $292.8M: the daily print and the weekly trend disagree, which means the ETH ETF story is one day of selling inside a otherwise buying week, not a reversal. Whale activity over the last 24 hours shows $48.2M moving onto exchanges on net, with BTC alone contributing $76.9M onto Binance, partly offset by $28.7M in CRO moving off Cryptocom. Zoom out to the weekly whale series and every one of the last four weeks (Aug 25, Sep 01, Sep 08, Sep 15) shows net flow onto exchanges, ranging from $49M to $1.2B. Coins moving toward exchanges in size, across four straight weeks, sits alongside a stablecoin float that's only grown 1.34% over 30 days to $310.3B: the dry powder isn't building nearly as fast as coins are heading toward venues where they can be sold.

Sentiment is the outlier in the room. Fear & Greed reads 69, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 31 to 74, on a day where total market cap fell 6.28% and every major asset is red. The crowd's mood gauge hasn't caught up with the tape, or the tape hasn't caught up with a crowd that's still feeling good from the monthly gains. Either way, that gap between a Greed reading and a broad daily selloff is worth sitting with rather than explaining away.

Worth watching from here: whether BTC and ETH hold their 200-day lines through this drawdown or join DOGE and ADA below them, whether the negative funding on ETH and SOL persists or flips back positive, whether the weekly whale-flow series produces its first net inflow week after four straight outflow weeks, and whether the BTC ETF five-session outflow trend extends or reverses on the next print.
